The Basics

Three Worlds of Wine

Explore the essentials of red, white, and sparkling wine — click any card to discover its unique character.

Bold & Complex

Red Wine

Made from dark-skinned grapes — gets its color, tannins, and depth from extended skin contact during fermentation.

Crisp & Fresh

White Wine

Crafted from green or yellow grapes, ranging from bone-dry to lusciously sweet with vibrant, refreshing acidity.

Festive & Fun

Sparkling Wine

Bubbles from secondary fermentation create that iconic effervescence. Champagne is the most celebrated style.

    Sommelier Tips

    Serving Guide

    Two things that dramatically affect how wine tastes before it even touches your tongue: the temperature it's served at, and the glass it's served in.

    Serving Temperature

    Serving wine at the right temperature unlocks its full aroma and flavor. Too cold and aromas are muted; too warm and alcohol dominates.

    Glassware

    The shape of the glass is based on science and dramatically affects the aroma — it determines how the wine reaches your nose and how quickly it warms up.

    Red Wine Glass
    Features a large, wide bowl — red wine needs a large surface area to breathe, which releases its bold fruit aromas and softens its structure.
    White Wine Glass
    Features a smaller, U-shaped bowl — the narrower opening keeps the wine cool longer and prevents the temperature from rising too fast.
    Sparkling Wine Flute
    The tall, skinny flute lets you enjoy the long streams of rising bubbles. However, for complex, expensive Champagne, experts recommend a white wine glass to better reveal its rich aromas.

    💡 Expert tip: When drinking a premium, aged Champagne, try it in a white wine glass instead of a flute — the wider bowl lets you smell the full complexity of its aromas.
